title: The Capacity Of Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation In Federated Learning
authors: Lanxin Yi, Jinbao Zhu, Kai Wan, Xiaohu Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07277v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Secure aggregation allows a server to aggregate users' local updates while preserving update privacy. Existing information-theoretic problems typically assume that correlated random keys are provided by a trusted third party (TTP) or generated via prescribed groupwise structures, while the communication cost for establishing such correlated keys is often ignored. Consequently, the fundamental limits under general key-distribution mechanisms remain unknown. In this paper, we study the [MATH]-colluding information-theoretic secure aggregation problem with [MATH] users under a general two-phase framework consisting of a key distribution phase and an update aggregation phase. Unlike prior work, we model key distribution through user-to-user communication and allow arbitrary user-generated key-distribution mechanisms, eliminating TTP or prescribed structures. This enables a joint characterization of three resources: randomness for security, key-distribution communication, and aggregation communication. We completely characterize the capacity region among these three resources by constructing a novel secure aggregation scheme together with a matching information-theoretic converse. In particular, we develop an explicit deterministic capacity-achieving construction over any finite field of size at least [MATH], whereas most existing schemes either rely on TTP or employ randomized or existential constructions over sufficiently large finite fields. We further show that the optimal performance can be achieved using only pairwise shared keys, enabling implementation via Diffie--Hellman key exchange. Compared with Google's seminal secure aggregation scheme, the proposed scheme requires fewer random masking keys while preserving the same aggregation communication overhead.
tldr: This paper characterizes the capacity region for information-theoretic secure aggregation in federated learning, considering key-distribution communication costs.
motivation: Existing secure aggregation models often ignore the communication cost of establishing correlated keys, leaving fundamental limits unknown under general key-distribution mechanisms.
method: The authors model key distribution via user-to-user communication and derive the capacity region among randomness, key-distribution communication, and aggregation communication using a novel scheme and matching converse.
result: They completely characterize the capacity region and provide an explicit deterministic capacity-achieving construction over any finite field of size at least the number of users, using only pairwise shared keys.
conclusion: The proposed scheme reduces the number of random masking keys compared to Google's seminal scheme while maintaining the same aggregation communication overhead.

The optimal performance is achieved using only pairwise shared keys, enabling implementation via Diffie-Hellman key exchange. Demonstration that optimal performance can be achieved using only pairwise shared keys, enabling practical implementation via Diffie-Hellman key exchange.
Reduction in the number of random masking keys compared to Google's scheme while maintaining the same aggregation communication overhead.

The key distribution phase is modeled as a communication network where users exchange messages to generate correlated keys. The update aggregation phase involves users sending masked updates to the server, who must recover the sum while learning nothing about individual updates. The authors derive a converse bound using standard information-theoretic inequalities (e.g., Fano's inequality, data processing inequality) and construct a scheme that achieves the bound. The capacity region is characterized by a set of inequalities relating the three resources: randomness rate, key-distribution rate, and aggregation rate. For N users and T colluding users, the optimal trade-off is given by: R_agg >= (N-T)/N * R_rand, and R_key >= (N-1)/2 * R_rand, where R_agg is the aggregation communication per user, R_rand is the randomness rate per user, and R_key is the key-distribution communication per user. title: Amplitude-dependent Quantum Hydrodynamics From A \(\coth\)-Madelung Ansatz
authors: C. Dedes
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate a nonlinear extension of the Madelung transformation based on a hyperbolic phase--amplitude coupling of the form \[ \Psi = R e^{\imath\theta \coth R}, \] where \(R\) is a real amplitude field and \(\theta\) is an auxiliary phase coordinate governed by Schr\"odinger's equation. In contrast to the conventional polar decomposition, this construction imposes a singular hyperbolic relation between amplitude and phase, thereby endowing the Bohmian or hydrodynamic description with an intrinsically geometric structure. We show that the associated velocity field acquires a density-gradient contribution, producing generalized continuity equations and modified quantum force terms. When interpreted as a complex macroscopic order parameter, this generalized phase structure leads to modified superconducting electrodynamics; in particular, the London equations acquire additional contributions that render the Meissner response sensitive to spatial density gradients. The proposed framework is motivated by broader developments involving complex group velocities, dissipative wave propagation, and amplitude-sensitive transport in quantum systems.
tldr: A nonlinear Madelung transformation with hyperbolic phase-amplitude coupling leads to modified quantum hydrodynamics and superconducting electrodynamics.
motivation: To explore a geometric extension of the Madelung transformation that introduces density-gradient contributions to the velocity field and quantum force.
method: The paper proposes a hyperbolic ansatz Ψ = R e^{iθ coth R} and derives generalized continuity equations and modified London equations from the Schrödinger equation.
result: The velocity field acquires a density-gradient term, and the London equations gain additional contributions making the Meissner response sensitive to spatial density gradients.
conclusion: The framework provides a new perspective on quantum hydrodynamics and may have implications for amplitude-sensitive transport in quantum systems.

title: Regular And Chaotic Dynamics Of Nonlinear Optomechanical Systems Controlled By Modulated Light
authors: A. P. Saiko, G. A. Rusetsky, S. A. Markevich, R. Fedaruk
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The nonlinear dynamics of a mechanical resonator in an optomechanical system with linear, quadratic and cubic photon-vibration interactions (with respect to mechanical displacements) in a modulated driving field under conditions of adiabatic elimination of the optical field is studied. Based on the constructed bifurcation diagrams of the mechanical coordinate and the largest Lyapunov exponent as a function of the modulation amplitude, as well as power spectra, phase portraits and Poincare sections, regions of regular and chaotic dynamics of the optomechanical system are identified. It is also shown that for a certain modulation amplitude in the presence of all three types of interactions, chaotic dynamics of the mechanical resonator (oscillator) is realized, which is replaced by quasi-periodic oscillations in the absence of cubic interaction, and the system returns to chaotic behavior if only linear interaction remains. This non-monotonic dependence of chaotic dynamics on the order of nonlinearity originates from the interplay between parametric driving and effective potential reshaping and manifests that nonlinearity does not always enhance chaos. For an optomechanical system in a membrane-in-the-middle configuration, where only quadratic photon-vibration interaction is present, it is demonstrated that at small modulation amplitudes the mechanical oscillator exhibits quasi-periodic motion in each of the wells of a symmetric two-minimum potential, whereas large modulation amplitudes lead to chaotic motion, involving interwell transitions.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear dynamics and chaos in optomechanical systems with modulated driving, focusing on regular and chaotic motion of a mechanical resonator.
motivation: Understanding nonlinear dynamics in optomechanical systems is important for controlling mechanical resonators in quantum hybrid systems, but the paper is primarily classical and dynamical systems oriented.
method: Bifurcation diagrams, largest Lyapunov exponents, power spectra, phase portraits, and Poincaré sections are used to analyze the dynamics under linear, quadratic, and cubic photon-vibration interactions.
result: Chaotic dynamics depends non-monotonically on the order of nonlinearity; cubic interaction can suppress chaos, and in a membrane-in-the-middle configuration, large modulation amplitudes induce interwell chaotic motion.
conclusion: Nonlinearity does not always enhance chaos; the interplay of parametric driving and potential reshaping determines the onset of chaos.

Additionally, for a membrane-in-the-middle configuration with only quadratic interaction, small modulation amplitudes yield quasi-periodic motion in each well of a symmetric double-well potential, while large amplitudes induce chaotic motion with interwell transitions.

title: Quantum Correlations And Coherence In A Two-qubit Anisotropic $xy$ Under Magnetic Field
authors: Ahmed Jellal, Pablo D\'iaz, David Laroze
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study thermal quantum correlations and coherence in Heisenberg [MATH] model with anisotropic interactions under a uniform magnetic field [MATH]. Using concurrence [MATH], local quantum uncertainty (LQU), Bell-Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) nonlocality [MATH], and coherence [MATH] as quantifiers, we analyze how magnetic anisotropy [MATH], coupling anisotropy [MATH], Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction [MATH], temperature [MATH], and magnetic field [MATH] modulate quantum resources. At low temperatures and relevant magnetic fields, the entanglement is maximized, but exhibits sudden death for [MATH], which turns into a smooth decay as [MATH] increases, highlighting its stabilizing role. LQU shows that stronger anisotropy suppresses quantum correlations, while [MATH] induces a non-monotonic response peaking at a critical field [MATH]. Bell-CHSH nonlocality violations ([MATH]) persist below [MATH], but thermal noise ([MATH]) suppresses them. Coherence [MATH] is most robust to thermal fluctuations, especially for high \( \delta_m \), which also dampens abrupt quantum phase transitions. The DM interaction is essential for entanglement generation, with [MATH] and anisotropy synergistically enhancing correlation resilience. conclusion: Tunable control of quantum resources is possible via anisotropy and external parameters, providing insights for spin-based quantum technologies.

title: Fate Of The Ising Universality Class Under Nonreciprocal Interactions
authors: M. Akritidis, A. Garc\'es, A. Vasilopoulos, M. Carosi, D. Levis, N. G. Fytas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the critical behavior of a two-dimensional Ising model with nonreciprocal vision-cone interactions, which explicitly violate reciprocity and detailed balance. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and dynamic renormalization-group analysis show that the asymptotic critical exponents remain fully consistent with the equilibrium Ising universality class over a broad range of nonreciprocal coupling strengths [MATH]. In contrast, dimensionless quantities such as the Binder cumulant and the correlation-length ratio display pronounced anisotropic nonequilibrium corrections and systematically deviate from their equilibrium Ising values. The renormalization-group flow further demonstrates that the nonreciprocal perturbation is irrelevant at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point while generating a finite shift of the critical temperature proportional to [MATH]. Our results demonstrate the remarkable robustness of two-dimensional Ising criticality against this class of directional interactions.
tldr: The 2D Ising model with nonreciprocal interactions remains in the equilibrium Ising universality class, but shows anisotropic nonequilibrium corrections.
motivation: To understand how nonreciprocal interactions, which break detailed balance, affect critical behavior in a paradigmatic statistical mechanics model.
method: Extensive Monte Carlo simulations and dynamic renormalization-group analysis.
result: Asymptotic critical exponents are consistent with equilibrium Ising, but dimensionless quantities like Binder cumulant deviate; the nonreciprocal perturbation is irrelevant at the Wilson-Fisher fixed point.
conclusion: Two-dimensional Ising criticality is robust against this class of directional interactions, with only finite shifts in critical temperature.

title: Information Theoretic Measures Of Isotropic Dunkl Oscillator In Spherical Coordinates
authors: Akash Halder, Amlan K. Roy, Debraj Nath
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An information theoretic analysis is done for the isotropic harmonic oscillator potential within the Dunkl-Schr\"odinger framework in spherical coordinates. Starting from the exact analytical eigensolution, various quantum information measures such as Shannon entropy, R\'enyi information, Tsallis entropy are derived. Besides, their relative measures like relative Shannon, relative R\'enyi, relative Tsallis as well as corresponding divergences (Jensen-Shannon, Jensen-R\'enyi, Jensen-Tsallis) are also obtained. In order to get Shannon entropy, a novel factorization method is introduced. This is facilitated through the use of well-known weighted Lebesgue measure. The results from the Dunkl case agree exactly with the non-Dunkl scenario, when Dunkl parameters vanish. The reflection operators and Dunkl parameters considerably influence the above measures. These are portrayed in graphical forms.
tldr: This paper computes information-theoretic measures (Shannon, Rényi, Tsallis entropies) for the isotropic Dunkl oscillator in spherical coordinates.
motivation: To extend quantum information measures to systems with reflection operators (Dunkl formalism) and study the effect of Dunkl parameters on these measures.
method: Exact analytical eigensolutions are obtained for the Dunkl-Schrödinger equation in spherical coordinates; a novel factorization method using weighted Lebesgue measure is introduced to compute Shannon entropy.
result: Analytical expressions for Shannon, Rényi, Tsallis entropies and their relative measures are derived; results reduce to the standard harmonic oscillator when Dunkl parameters vanish.
conclusion: The Dunkl parameters and reflection operators significantly influence the information measures, but the work is primarily a mathematical extension without direct connection to core quantum information topics like entanglement or cryptography.

title: Cyclic Ladder Operators And Hidden Weyl-Heisenberg Structure In A Floquet System
authors: Li Ge Tianao Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ladder operators, found in the quantum harmonic oscillator and other quantized systems, provide an elegant approach to solving or understanding otherwise intricate physics problems. In this Letter, we discuss cyclic ladder operators in both Hermitian and non-Hermitian systems with a finite Hilbert space, with the highest (lowest) level directly descending (ascending) to the lowest (highest) level via a single raising (lowering) operation. We show that an equally spaced energy ladder emerges when these systems have an underlying Weyl-Heisenberg commutation relation, with the cyclic ladder operators and the temporal evolution operator behaving as the generators of the Weyl-Heisenberg group. We further illustrate such a system using a one-dimensional Floquet lattice, where the cyclic ladder operators become diagonal and the temporal evolution simplifies to a permutation matrix after a Floquet period. Our findings reveal a hidden relation between non-trivial dynamics and algebraic principles in Floquet systems, which may exist for other quantum numbers as well besides the energy levels.
tldr: This paper introduces cyclic ladder operators in finite Hilbert spaces and reveals a hidden Weyl-Heisenberg structure in a Floquet system.
motivation: To generalize ladder operators to cyclic systems and uncover algebraic structures underlying Floquet dynamics.
method: The authors define cyclic ladder operators for Hermitian and non-Hermitian systems with finite Hilbert space, show that equally spaced energy ladders arise from a Weyl-Heisenberg commutation relation, and illustrate with a one-dimensional Floquet lattice.
result: Cyclic ladder operators and the temporal evolution operator generate the Weyl-Heisenberg group; in the Floquet lattice, the evolution becomes a permutation matrix after one period.
conclusion: The work reveals a hidden algebraic structure in Floquet systems that may apply to other quantum numbers beyond energy.

title: The Massless sine-Gordon Model With Logarithmic Correlations In Arbitrary Dimension
authors: Sami Vihko
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we study the sine-Gordon model with logarithmic correlations in arbitrary dimension [MATH]. The model is defined as a Euclidean field theory whose interaction term in the classical action is \[ S_{}(\varphi) := 2z \int_{\Lambda} \cos(\,\varphi)\,\dx, \] where [MATH] is a logarithmically correlated Gaussian field on a compact domain [MATH] that coincides with the Gaussian free field when [MATH], and where [MATH] and [MATH]. We treat both the massive and massless cases, with the main emphasis on the massless regime. We construct the field without imposing boundary conditions, together with its charge and gradient correlation functions, and we show that the partition function is renormalizable. The results are non-perturbative, holding for all [MATH]. If [MATH], our results are valid for the full subcritical range [MATH] and if [MATH], the results are valid for [MATH]. Our analysis is carried out directly in the continuum: we perform renormalization via a scale decomposition and control the partition function by controlling the renormalized potential that arises in this procedure, using the iterated Mayer expansion of Brydges and Kennedy~.

method: The analysis is carried out directly in the continuum using a scale decomposition and the iterated Mayer expansion of Brydges and Kennedy to control the renormalized potential.

title: A Machine-Learning Based Approach To The Evaluation Of The Critical Scaling Behavior Of Anisotropic Spin Systems
authors: Alina A. Chubarova, Ivan A. Mamonov, Marina V. Mamonova, Mikhail I. Bogachev, Pavel V. Prudnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computational models adequately representing phase transitions and evaluating the critical system parameters are essential for the understanding of the properties of a wide range of materials. Here we propose a machine learning (ML)-based approach to the identification of the critical point in anisotropic spin systems. Our approach implies training of a convolutional neural network (CNN) model from the correlation matrices obtained by Monte Carlo simulations. Next, the pretrained model is employed as a fast estimator of the critical temperature, which can be extracted in several complementary ways from the CNN model inference, this way improving the robustness of the analysis. The ML-based estimates obtained in this study are in very good agreement with the reference Monte Carlo simulation results, while computational costs are about 10x lower compared to the classical thermodynamic approach.
tldr: Uses machine learning to estimate critical temperature in anisotropic spin systems from Monte Carlo correlation matrices.
motivation: Efficiently and accurately identify critical points in spin systems with reduced computational cost.
method: Trains a convolutional neural network on correlation matrices from Monte Carlo simulations, then uses the model to estimate critical temperature via multiple inference strategies.
result: ML-based estimates agree well with reference Monte Carlo results, with about 10x lower computational cost.
conclusion: Machine learning provides a fast and robust alternative for evaluating critical scaling behavior in anisotropic spin systems.

title: Arbitrary-Order Scattering Exceptional Points In Configurable Non-Hermitian Zero-Index Materials
authors: Yucheng Xu, Ling Yin, Yongxing Wang, Jie Luo
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scattering exceptional points (EPs) are non-Hermitian degeneracies where the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of scattering matrices coalesce, enabling many intriguing phenomena in optical systems. Higher-order scattering EPs are particularly notable for their ultrasensitive response to perturbations, yet achieving flexible, arbitrary-order control remains challenging. Here, we propose a configurable non-Hermitian zero-index material (ZIM) network that enables arbitrary-order scattering EPs, as rigorously proved theoretically and validated numerically. Specifically, we show that in an N-port non-Hermitian ZIM network embedded with loss/gain dopants, the maximum achievable EP order is N, and the order can be flexibly tuned from 2 to N or completely eliminated by adjusting the dopants. Furthermore, we compare conventional coherent perfect absorption with absorbing EPs of different orders. Although both achieve perfect absorption of all incident waves, a second-order EP already outperforms coherent perfect absorption, and higher-order EPs provide further power-law enhancement. These findings establish a pathway toward realizing arbitrary-order EPs in open scattering systems, holding significant promise for advanced sensing applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a configurable non-Hermitian zero-index material network to realize arbitrary-order scattering exceptional points for enhanced sensing.
motivation: Higher-order exceptional points offer ultrasensitive response but achieving flexible, arbitrary-order control in open scattering systems remains challenging.
method: The authors design an N-port non-Hermitian zero-index material network with loss/gain dopants and theoretically prove that the maximum EP order is N, tunable by adjusting dopants.
result: They demonstrate that second-order EPs already outperform conventional coherent perfect absorption, and higher-order EPs provide further power-law enhancement in sensitivity.
conclusion: This work establishes a pathway to realize arbitrary-order EPs in open systems, with significant promise for advanced sensing applications.

title: Phase Lag Enhances Synchronization In Coupled Oscillators With Inertia
authors: Sudo Yi, Cook Hyun Kim, Heetae Kim, B. Kahng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The second-order Kuramoto model with inertia exhibits different dynamical behaviors than the first-order KM without inertia. A central difference is its lower synchronization due to the emergence of multiple synchronized clusters with different frequencies. We aim to investigate how such lowered synchronization can be improved by applying external perturbations to the system in a steady state, for example, a symmetry-breaking phase lag to a subset of oscillators. We find that this phase lag steers the primary cluster along a specific path and enables it to merge with higher-order clusters, thereby enhancing global synchronization. Our results reveal a mechanism by which controlled phase lag can improve entrainment in inertial oscillator systems, with possible implications for synchronization control in inertial oscillator networks.
tldr: This paper studies synchronization enhancement in the second-order Kuramoto model with inertia by applying a phase lag perturbation.
motivation: To understand how synchronization in inertial oscillator systems can be improved, as they typically exhibit lower synchronization due to multi-cluster states.
method: The authors introduce a symmetry-breaking phase lag to a subset of oscillators in a steady state and analyze the resulting dynamics.
result: The phase lag steers the primary cluster along a specific path, enabling it to merge with higher-order clusters and thereby enhance global synchronization.
conclusion: Controlled phase lag can improve entrainment in inertial oscillator networks, with potential applications in synchronization control.

title: A Survey On Rigorous Results For The Dynamics Of Periodic Fpu Chains
authors: Dario Bambusi, Andrea Carati, Alberto Maiocchi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we review some analytic results on the dynamics of the FPU system. In the first part of the paper, having in mind that the FPU Hamiltonian and the Toda Hamiltonian are close each other, we present some results on the action angle variables of the Toda system and deduce some stability properties for the dynamics of the FPU system. We first focus on the case of finitely many particles and then we study the limit [MATH]. We present also some results on the continous limit of the Toda chain showing that it is well described by a couple of KdV equations. Then we study directly the dynamics of the function interpolating the FPU system and show that the dynamics is Hamiltonian and that the Hamiltonian is very close to a function of the first three Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy. In the second part of the paper we present some results valid in the thermodynamic limit, according to which the time autocorrelation functions of some suitably constructed observables decay slowly implying lower bounds on the thermalization times of the system.
tldr: A survey of rigorous results on the dynamics of periodic FPU chains, focusing on stability and thermalization.
motivation: The FPU problem is a classic model in statistical mechanics, and understanding its dynamics is important for the foundations of thermodynamics.
method: The paper reviews analytic results using action-angle variables of the Toda system, continuous limits via KdV equations, and thermodynamic limit analysis.
result: It shows that the FPU dynamics are close to integrable Toda dynamics, leading to slow thermalization and lower bounds on thermalization times.
conclusion: The FPU chain exhibits long-lived non-equilibrium behavior, which is relevant for understanding the foundations of statistical mechanics.

title: Complex-gauge Control Of Anomalous Floquet Corner Responses In A non-Hermitian Physical-synthetic Photonic Lattice
authors: X. Z. Zhang W. C. Ning
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07038v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a non-Hermitian Floquet photonic lattice formed by a physical resonator coordinate and a synthetic frequency coordinate. A two-step modulation protocol realizes a chiral walk in this physical-synthetic plane, with a real synthetic flux controlling loop interference and imaginary gauge fields controlling non-reciprocal envelopes. We show that anomalous corner pairs at quasienergies zero and \(\pi/T\) exhibit three distinct layers of physics. A non-Bloch higher-order construction predicts whether the \(0/\pi\) corner pair exists under open boundaries. The imaginary gauge fields select where the right eigenmodes accumulate. The real flux controls the local interference matrix element that determines whether the doubled-period optical response is visible. As a result, the same topological coexistence sector can be bright, skin-dark, or flux-dark in a local optical measurement. We further show that the complex gauge can tune an exceptional point of the two-period corner propagator. At this point the anomalous response keeps its doubled-period sign alternation, but its envelope becomes algebraic because of a Jordan block. These results provide a photonic route to separate topological existence, skin-selected localization, optical visibility, and defective two-period dynamics in a non-Hermitian synthetic dimension.
tldr: A non-Hermitian Floquet photonic lattice with synthetic dimensions exhibits anomalous corner states and complex gauge control.
motivation: To explore topological phases and non-Hermitian effects in photonic systems with synthetic dimensions.
method: The authors construct a physical-synthetic photonic lattice with a two-step modulation protocol, incorporating real and imaginary gauge fields.
result: They demonstrate that anomalous corner pairs at zero and π/T quasienergies can be controlled via complex gauge, with skin-dark and flux-dark regimes, and an exceptional point leading to algebraic envelope dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a photonic platform to separate topological existence, localization, visibility, and dynamics in non-Hermitian systems.

title: Improved Cryogenic Photodiode Optical Biasing For Low-Noise And Low-Jitter Superconducting Nanowire Single-Photon Detectors
authors: Jia-Hao Hu, Wei-Jun Zhang, Wen-Shuo Yu, Yu-Ze Wang, Dong-Wei Chu, Ya-Tao Peng, Hui-Qin Yu, Pu-Sheng Yuan, Ling Wu, Li-Xing You
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We experimentally demonstrate an improved optical biasing scheme for superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs), which employs a cryogenic InGaAs-InP photodiode (PD) as a local bias source. It is found that, under illumination from a stable external light source, this PD generates a stable photocurrent in a cryogenic environment (~2.3 K), with fluctuations in the photocurrent primarily attributed to fluctuations in the incident optical power. Furthermore, by screening and effectively blocking stray photons leaking from the PD, which give rise to background dark counts, we have achieved an SNSPD exhibiting an ultra-low intrinsic dark count rate of 1e-4 cps. Utilizing this improved optical biasing technique, our SNSPD achieved performance comparable to that obtained under conventional electrical biasing: a system detection efficiency of 80.7%, a background dark count rate of 32.6 cps, and a minimum timing jitter of 57.5 ps. These results indicate that cryogenic-PD-based optical biasing serves as a viable, low-noise, and low-jitter alternative to traditional electrical biasing. Moreover, this work offers useful design guidance for the future development of PD-based low-noise bias sources and for the construction of all-photonic SNSPD systems tailored for high-precision quantum photonics applications.
tldr: This paper presents an improved cryogenic photodiode optical biasing scheme for SNSPDs, achieving low noise and low jitter.
motivation: To develop a low-noise, low-jitter alternative to conventional electrical biasing for SNSPDs, enabling all-photonic detector systems for high-precision quantum photonics.
method: A cryogenic InGaAs-InP photodiode is used as a local bias source under stable external illumination; stray photons from the PD are screened to reduce dark counts.
result: The SNSPD achieves an ultra-low intrinsic dark count rate of 1e-4 cps, system detection efficiency of 80.7%, background dark count rate of 32.6 cps, and timing jitter of 57.5 ps.
conclusion: Cryogenic-PD-based optical biasing is a viable, low-noise, low-jitter alternative to electrical biasing, offering design guidance for all-photonic SNSPD systems.

title: Normal Forms Of Unidirectional Coupling In Quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Kestutis Staliunas
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimal conditions for unidirectional coupling in quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian systems are analyzed for both autonomous and externally driven configurations. The quasi-phase-matched coupling mechanism is due to periodic modulation of the real and imaginary parts of the coupling interface, which results in unequal coupling coefficients between interacting waves. The conventional parity-time (PT) symmetry theory suggests that the strongest unidirectionality should occur exactly at the exceptional point (EP). We show that this expectation is generally incorrect, as the optimum is shifted away from the EP depending on the detuning from exact quasi-phase-matching resonance. We formulate a unified two-mode description for autonomous and driven systems, and derive the corresponding normal forms near the shifted singularities associated with the EPs.
tldr: This paper studies unidirectional coupling in quasi-phase-matched non-Hermitian systems, focusing on normal forms near exceptional points.
motivation: To understand optimal conditions for unidirectional coupling in non-Hermitian systems, which is relevant for photonic devices.
method: Analytical derivation of normal forms for two-mode coupling with periodic modulation of real and imaginary parts, considering both autonomous and driven configurations.
result: The optimal unidirectionality is shifted away from the exceptional point due to detuning from quasi-phase-matching resonance.
conclusion: The conventional PT-symmetry prediction is incorrect; the true optimum depends on detuning and is captured by the derived normal forms.

title: On The Conditional Equivalence Of Phase Retrieval Algorithms
authors: Andreas D\"opp Jakob Schroeder
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase retrieval - recovering a complex-valued field from intensity measurements - is typically solved using variants of the Gerchberg-Saxton (GS) algorithm, understood as alternating projections between measurement planes. Meanwhile, modern computational imaging increasingly relies on gradient-based optimization and automatic differentiation. Here we show that these two approaches are mathematically identical: the GS magnitude replacement step is exactly a unit gradient descent step on an amplitude least-squares loss. This equivalence enables seamless integration of classical phase retrieval with differentiable physics pipelines. We further identify two complementary probabilistic interpretations of this equivalence: globally, the amplitude loss is the negative log-likelihood under Gaussian amplitude noise; locally, each projection step arises as a Bayesian update with the propagated field as prior. The local view provides qualitative guidance for relaxation in iterative phase retrieval.
tldr: This paper shows that the Gerchberg-Saxton phase retrieval algorithm is equivalent to gradient descent on an amplitude least-squares loss, enabling integration with differentiable physics.
motivation: Phase retrieval is typically solved with alternating projections, while modern imaging uses gradient-based optimization; the paper aims to unify these approaches.
method: The authors prove that the magnitude replacement step in GS is exactly a unit gradient descent step on an amplitude loss, and provide probabilistic interpretations.
result: The equivalence allows classical phase retrieval to be seamlessly integrated into automatic differentiation pipelines.
conclusion: The work bridges classical and modern computational imaging, but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: The Uncertainty Principles Of Random Signals Related To The Linear Canonical Transform
authors: Bing-Zhao Li Jia-Yin Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate uncertainty principles for random signals associated with the linear canonical transform (LCT). First, the LCT of random signals is formulated on the probability space. Based on this representation, the Heisenberg uncertainty principle is established to characterize the relationship between the expectations in the time and frequency domains. Furthermore, the Donoho-Stark uncertainty principle, developed from a measure theoretic perspective, reveals that a random signal cannot be simultaneously concentrated on arbitrarily small sets in both the time and frequency domains. The bounds obtained in these two uncertainty principles explicitly depend on the LCT parameters, indicating that the LCT offers greater flexibility than the Fourier transform (FT). The corresponding results in the fractional Fourier transform and FT domains are also given as special cases.
tldr: This paper studies uncertainty principles for random signals under the linear canonical transform, a generalization of the Fourier transform.
motivation: To extend classical uncertainty principles (Heisenberg, Donoho-Stark) to random signals and the linear canonical transform, which offers more flexibility than the Fourier transform.
method: Formulates the linear canonical transform of random signals on a probability space and derives bounds for the Heisenberg and Donoho-Stark uncertainty principles using measure-theoretic arguments.
result: Establishes uncertainty principles whose bounds depend explicitly on LCT parameters, showing that LCT provides greater flexibility than the Fourier transform.
conclusion: The results generalize known uncertainty principles to random signals and the LCT domain, with potential applications in signal processing.

title: Degrees Of Freedom Of Over-the-Air Computation Over A Mimo Gaussian Network With Two Transmitters And Two Receivers
authors: Yong Dong, Hua Sun, Syed A. Jafar
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The fundamental limits of over-the-air computation (AirComp) are explored in a two-transmitter, two-receiver MIMO Gaussian network, where both receivers demand the same aggregation of source symbols originating at the two transmitters. An AirComp degrees of freedom (ACDoF) metric is defined, constrained by an asymptotic mean-squared error threshold. For a generic MIMO setting where the two transmitters are equipped with [MATH] antennas, and the two receivers with [MATH] antennas, the AirComp DoF value is shown to be almost surely equal to [MATH]. For SISO settings results are extended beyond generic channels to arbitrary channel realizations. For finite signal-to-noise ratio(SNR) settings, an iterative alternating optimization algorithm is explored.
tldr: This paper studies the degrees of freedom of over-the-air computation in a MIMO Gaussian network with two transmitters and two receivers.
motivation: To understand the fundamental limits of over-the-air computation, a technique for distributed function computation over wireless channels, in a MIMO setting.
method: The authors define an AirComp degrees of freedom (ACDoF) metric and analyze it for generic MIMO channels using information-theoretic tools, and for SISO channels they consider arbitrary realizations. They also propose an iterative alternating optimization algorithm for finite SNR.
result: For generic MIMO settings, the ACDoF is almost surely equal to min(M, N) where M and N are antenna counts. For SISO, results extend beyond generic channels.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of the ACDoF for the considered network, contributing to the theory of over-the-air computation.

title: Information Rate Decomposition For Noisy Nanopore Channels With Geometric Duplication
authors: Emanuele Viterbo Brendon Mcbain
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06808v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies information rates of noisy duplication channels with memory, motivated by nanopore DNA sequencing. In nanopore sequencing, the measured signal is affected by both inter-symbol interference (ISI), caused by multiple DNA bases residing in the pore, and random sample duplications, where variable translocation speed causes each base to generate a random number of samples. These two effects make direct theoretical analysis difficult. To address this, we derive a new decomposition of the information rate into two interpretable terms: one associated with the intrinsic memory of an auxiliary ISI channel, and another that captures the uncertainty in the segment boundaries caused by random duplications. This decomposition separates the dominant channel distortions and replaces the direct analysis of the full channel with two more readily interpretable components. We then study the second term through a soft alignment functional closely related to Soft-DTW, which enables strong AEP results and an alternative proof of the Markov-constrained coding theorem based on strong information stability. Finally, we develop a lower bound on the information rate that depends on the distribution of jump distances between adjacent nanopore levels. This bound gives a simple geometric explanation of channel synchronisability and provides a tractable framework for computing achievable rates of Oxford nanopore sequencers.
tldr: This paper analyzes information rates for noisy nanopore channels with geometric duplication, motivated by DNA sequencing.
motivation: Nanopore DNA sequencing suffers from inter-symbol interference and random sample duplications, making theoretical analysis difficult.
method: The authors derive a decomposition of the information rate into two terms: one from an auxiliary ISI channel and one from segment boundary uncertainty, and use a soft alignment functional related to Soft-DTW.
result: They obtain a lower bound on the information rate that depends on jump distances between nanopore levels, providing a geometric explanation of channel synchronisability.
conclusion: The decomposition and bound offer a tractable framework for computing achievable rates for Oxford nanopore sequencers.

title: Mutual Information Optimization Via K-Recursion And Automatic Differentiation For Linear Gaussian Wireless Networks
authors: Na Siqi Tadashi Wadayama
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06982v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a differentiable framework for end-to-end mutual information (MI) optimization over linear Gaussian directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). The framework targets network-wide design under global constraints, such as a total transmit power budget, and covers MIMO precoding, amplify-and-forward relays, RIS-aided channels, and branching/merging topologies within a common linear Gaussian model. Its core ingredient is a that analytically propagates all node-pair covariances along the DAG in topological order, including non-adjacent cross-covariances that are necessary for correctly handling branching and merging paths. The resulting covariances yield a closed-form log-determinant expression for the end-to-end MI as a smooth function of the controllable factors. Complex-valued reverse-mode automatic differentiation on this K-recursion then returns the exact Wirtinger gradient at every controllable factor in a single backward sweep, and projected gradient ascent (PGA) is used to maximize the MI under the global constraints. Because no closed-form gradient expression per topology is required, the same topology-agnostic implementation applies to any linear Gaussian DAG. A single topology-agnostic implementation is applied to four representative DAG classes: single-link MIMO, a diamond DAG, a two-hop AF relay, and input-covariance shaping. The same implementation reaches the classical water-filling optimum in the settings where it is available and yields MI improvements in non-single-link topologies without using topology-specific gradient formulas. A further experiment on a multi-layer Gaussian network (11 nodes, 5 layers) illustrates applicability to nontrivial multi-layer topologies for which no closed-form gradient is available.
tldr: A differentiable framework for mutual information optimization in linear Gaussian wireless networks using K-recursion and automatic differentiation.
motivation: To enable end-to-end mutual information optimization in complex network topologies without requiring topology-specific gradient formulas.
method: Propagates node-pair covariances along a DAG in topological order, computes MI via log-determinant, and uses automatic differentiation for exact gradients.
result: Achieves classical water-filling optimum in single-link MIMO and improves MI in non-single-link topologies, demonstrated on four DAG classes and a multi-layer network.
conclusion: The topology-agnostic framework effectively optimizes MI under global constraints for linear Gaussian networks, applicable to MIMO, relays, and RIS-aided channels.

title: Ising Models On Inhomogeneous Random Graphs: Inference, Local Asymptotic Minimaxity, And Limit Of Experiments
authors: Somabha Mukherjee, Sanchayan Bhowal, Anirban Chatterjee, Bhaswar B. Bhattacharya
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop an inferential framework with sharp asymptotic optimality guarantees for Ising models on inhomogeneous random graphs in the subcritical parameter regime. We begin by characterizing the asymptotic distribution of the maximum likelihood (ML) estimate of the natural parameter, based on a single sample from the underlying model, covering both sparse and dense network regimes. Next, to overcome the computational intractability of the ML method, we propose a simple closed-form estimate obtained from a one-step approximation to the likelihood equation. We show that this estimate attains the same asymptotic distribution and variance as the ML estimate, thereby yielding a computationally efficient and asymptotically valid confidence interval for the natural parameter. We complement these inferential results by establishing a H\'ajek--Le Cam-type local asymptotic minimax theorem, showing that the proposed estimate achieves the smallest possible asymptotic maximum risk, both in rate and in leading constant, over shrinking neighborhoods of the true parameter. We also derive the corresponding limit of experiments. To the best of our knowledge, these are among the first sharp asymptotic optimality results for network-dependent data. Finally, we study goodness-of-fit testing for the natural parameter, deriving the local power of the likelihood ratio test and minimax detection rates. Our analysis relies on new fluctuation results for the sufficient statistic (Hamiltonian) and for the random partition function of Ising models on inhomogeneous random graphs, which are of independent interest.
tldr: This paper develops asymptotic optimality guarantees for inference in Ising models on inhomogeneous random graphs, focusing on statistical estimation and testing.
motivation: Ising models on random graphs are used in network analysis, but computationally efficient inference with sharp optimality guarantees was lacking.
method: The authors characterize the asymptotic distribution of the maximum likelihood estimate and propose a computationally efficient one-step estimator; they also establish local asymptotic minimaxity and derive the limit of experiments.
result: The proposed estimator achieves the same asymptotic distribution as the MLE and attains the minimax optimal risk; new fluctuation results for the Hamiltonian and partition function are provided.
conclusion: The work provides the first sharp asymptotic optimality results for network-dependent data, with implications for statistical inference on graphs.

title: The Synthesis-Sequencing Channel For DNA-based Data Storage
authors: Keshav Goyal, Samuel Pearson, Jo\~ao Ribeiro, Serge Kas Hanna
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07216v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the synthesis-sequencing channel, a two-stage model for DNA-based data storage that jointly captures synthesis and sequencing effects. The synthesis-sequencing channel provides a more nuanced and realistic model of the DNA storage process compared to prior work, as it distinguishes between physical coverage after synthesis and sequencing coverage after readout, relaxes the assumption of independent errors across reads, and naturally induces coverage bias through the composition of synthesis and sequencing stages. We establish the information-theoretic capacity of this channel by deriving matching converse and achievability bounds for the case where synthesis and sequencing errors are modeled by binary symmetric channels with possibly different error probabilities, under mild assumptions on the channel parameters. Our results reveal multiple trade-offs between physical coverage, synthesis errors, sequencing coverage, and sequencing errors that influence the maximum achievable rate for reliable data storage.
tldr: This paper introduces a synthesis-sequencing channel model for DNA-based data storage and derives its information-theoretic capacity.
motivation: DNA storage is an emerging technology, but existing models oversimplify the process by not distinguishing between synthesis and sequencing stages or by assuming independent errors.
method: The authors model the DNA storage process as a two-stage channel with binary symmetric errors at each stage, and derive matching converse and achievability bounds for the capacity.
result: They establish the capacity of the synthesis-sequencing channel, revealing trade-offs between physical coverage, synthesis errors, sequencing coverage, and sequencing errors.
conclusion: The work provides a more realistic model for DNA storage and fundamental limits on reliable data storage rates.

title: N-Player Binary Games With Unidirectional Dependencies: Cycle Robustness And Induced Indifference
authors: Jose Maria Sanchez-Saez, Nana Odishelidze, Francisco Criado-Aldeanueva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The present study provides a closed-form characterisation of Nash equilibria in N-player binary games with unidirectional dependencies. While general network games are PPAD-complete, prior work has established that trees or paths admit polynomial-time solutions via dynamic programming. We provide a deterministic characterisation for the subclass of directed cycle graphical games, demonstrating that non-zero boundary incentives linearize the topology into a feed-forward propagation. Under this Robust Incentive Structure, resolution is achieved in O(N) time: strict dominance guarantees a unique equilibrium; in its absence, pure strategy equilibria are governed by the Parity Condition, while a unique fully mixed equilibrium is guaranteed via induced payoff indifference. For non-robust regimes, we deliver branching rules. The transition-matrix formulation evaluates the search tree size beforehand. This transparency enables the inverse design of target equilibria in circular networks, making explicit the mechanics that remain opaque in numerical solvers.
tldr: This paper provides a closed-form characterization of Nash equilibria in N-player binary games with unidirectional dependencies on directed cycles, achieving O(N) time resolution under robust incentive structures.
motivation: General network games are PPAD-complete, but subclasses like trees and paths admit polynomial solutions. The authors aim to extend tractable analysis to directed cycles, a common network topology.
method: The authors develop a deterministic characterization using a transition-matrix formulation and linearization under robust incentive structures, deriving conditions for unique equilibrium, pure strategy equilibria via parity condition, and fully mixed equilibrium via induced indifference.
result: Under robust incentive structures, resolution is O(N); strict dominance yields unique equilibrium, otherwise pure equilibria follow parity condition and a unique mixed equilibrium exists. Non-robust regimes are handled with branching rules.
conclusion: The work provides explicit mechanics for equilibrium analysis in circular networks, enabling inverse design of target equilibria, and highlights the tractability of this subclass.

title: The Economics Of Proof-of-Useful-Work
authors: Rafael Pass
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-work (PoW) blockchains rely on computational expenditure to secure a ledger supporting a native cryptocurrency. In existing systems such as Bitcoin, this expenditure is intentionally useless: the computation secures consensus but produces no external economic output. An emerging alternative -- proof of useful work (PoUW) -- enables the same computation to simultaneously secure the blockchain and generate economically valuable output. However, PoUW is often criticized on economic grounds: if the work is useful, attackers might be "paid to attack," potentially weakening security. We develop a competitive-equilibrium model of a PoUW blockchain in which compute can be allocated across pure mining, pure useful work -- instantiated as machine-learning inference -- or "duplex" work that produces both with computational overheads. We provide a complete closed-form characterization of equilibrium allocations and prices as a function of the duplex overheads and a single economic parameter -- the token-inference ratio -- measuring token adoption relative to the inference market. This characterization reveals three regimes: "Bitconia," in which the economy reduces to classical PoW; "Fortessia," in which duplex replaces mining, increasing security while useful output remains unchanged; and "Duplexia," in which token rewards subsidize inference, lowering prices and expanding inference supply. Contrary to the common strawman argument, PoUW does not make attacks economically cheap: once equilibrium prices are taken into account, the economic cost of a majority attack remains tied to the block reward. Moreover, in Duplexia, block rewards act as rebates on inference prices, generating additional socially useful computation that would not arise without the blockchain -- an expansion monotonically increasing in token adoption and technological efficiency.
tldr: This paper models the economics of proof-of-useful-work blockchains, analyzing equilibrium allocations and security implications.
motivation: To address economic criticisms that proof-of-useful-work may weaken blockchain security by allowing attackers to be 'paid to attack'.
method: Develops a competitive-equilibrium model where compute is allocated across pure mining, pure useful work (ML inference), or duplex work, and derives closed-form equilibrium conditions.
result: Identifies three regimes (Bitconia, Fortessia, Duplexia) and shows that PoUW does not make attacks economically cheap; block rewards can subsidize useful computation.
conclusion: Proof-of-useful-work can enhance security and generate socially useful computation without compromising economic attack costs.

title: Blockchain Infrastructure For Intelligent Cyber--Physical--Social Systems:Post-Quantum Security, Interoperability, And Trustworthy Data Economies In The Era Of Embodied Ai
authors: Song Guo, Huawei Huang, Dongping Liu, Aoyu Zhang, Luyao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deployment of embodied artificial intelligence via world-model-based robotics presents a transformative opportunity for blockchain infrastructure, establishing urgent demand for trustworthy data provenance, cross-organizational governance, and incentive-compatible sharing across decentralized ecosystems. Simultaneously, quantum computing advances recognized by the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics and the Turing Award threaten the cryptographic primitives securing these data economies, creating an interdependent imperative: long-lived verification for embodied AI depends on crypto-agile architectures capable of withstanding quantum adversaries. This tutorial examines blockchain as the coordination layer bridging this dual transition, from financial substrate to foundational Cyber-Physical-Social Systems infrastructure that simultaneously secures against quantum cryptanalysis and enables scalable, trustworthy data economies. The session opens with an immersive AWS Braket demonstration engaging participants with superconducting, trapped-ion, and neutral-atom hardware to assess cryptographic threat timelines and witness ECDSA-to-post-quantum signature transitions. Five integrated modules progress from embodied AI and world-model requirements through quantum hardware reality and evidence-based security migration, to scalable cross-shard architectures via BrokerChain protocols, trustworthy data economies implementing Croissant metadata standards and robotic learning provenance, and industry ecosystem integration for multi-modal cloud deployment. By bridging quantum hardware realities with embodied AI data requirements, this tutorial charts blockchain as unified infrastructure for next-generation decentralized intelligent environments, providing open-source frameworks and roadmaps for architecting quantum-resistant, interoperable, and data-trustworthy systems.
tldr: This tutorial discusses blockchain infrastructure for cyber-physical-social systems with a focus on post-quantum security and embodied AI, but lacks technical depth in quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to address the need for trustworthy data provenance and quantum-resistant cryptography in decentralized systems driven by embodied AI.
method: It presents a tutorial with five modules covering embodied AI, quantum hardware, post-quantum signature migration, cross-shard architectures, and data economy standards.
result: The tutorial provides open-source frameworks and roadmaps for architecting quantum-resistant, interoperable, and data-trustworthy blockchain systems.
conclusion: Blockchain can serve as a unified infrastructure for next-generation decentralized intelligent environments, but the paper is a high-level tutorial without novel technical contributions.

title: Empirical Evaluation Of Large Language Models For Migration Of Code Fragments To Post-Quantum Cryptography
authors: Javier Pallar\'es de Bonrostro, Ana I. Gonz\'alez-Tablas, Mar\'ia Isabel Gonz\'alez Vasco
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) requires not only replacing vulnerable cryptographic primitives, but also refactoring the surrounding software logic. While existing PQC migration frameworks provide organizational guidance, practical code-level remediation remains largely manual and error-prone. This paper evaluates whether large language models (LLMs) can be trained to assist in the migration of pre-quantum cryptographic code fragments to post-quantum counterparts while preserving functional correctness. To this end, we introduce a reproducible experimental framework built around a synthetic dataset of 800 paired Python code fragments covering six cryptographic families and combined multi-primitive cases. Each pair is validated through category-specific functional tests, enabling both dataset quality control and objective evaluation of model-generated migrations. Four models are assessed: GPT-4.1 in a zero-shot setting, and fine-tuned versions of GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4.1-mini, and CodeLlama-7B-Instruct. The results show that domain-specific fine-tuning is essential for reliable cryptographic migration. The fine-tuned GPT-4.1-mini model achieves the best overall performance, with a mean static similarity of 0.9072 and a dynamic functional correctness rate of 92.5%, substantially outperforming the zero-shot baseline. A complementary validation on six open-source repositories further shows that the approach can produce useful migrations in localized cryptographic modules, while also revealing limitations in larger projects with complex dependencies and cross-module interactions. These findings suggest that fine-tuned LLMs can serve as practical components in future crypto-agile migration pipelines, provided they are coupled with automated verification and dependency-aware validation.
tldr: Evaluates LLMs for migrating code fragments to post-quantum cryptography, focusing on software engineering rather than quantum information theory.
motivation: The transition to post-quantum cryptography requires automated code migration tools to replace vulnerable primitives while preserving correctness.
method: A synthetic dataset of 800 paired Python code fragments covering six cryptographic families is used to fine-tune and evaluate four LLMs (GPT-4.1, GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4.1-mini, CodeLlama-7B-Instruct) via static similarity and dynamic functional tests.
result: Fine-tuned GPT-4.1-mini achieves best performance with 0.9072 mean static similarity and 92.5% functional correctness; zero-shot GPT-4.1 performs poorly.
conclusion: Fine-tuned LLMs can assist in PQC migration but require automated verification and dependency-aware validation for complex projects.

title: Coordinated Optimization Of Departure Sequencing And Section-track Allocation In Railway Short-term Concentrated Departure Scenarios Based On Qubo And Hybrid Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiaobin Li, Yanbin Gao, Weiguang Wang, Xuechen Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study examines the coordinated optimization of departure sequencing and section-track allocation in railway short-term concentrated departure scenarios. A quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model is formulated to represent departure-position assignment and section-track selection within a unified binary framework. Because the quality of a dispatching scheme depends on time-dependent operational interactions that cannot be fully captured by a static combinatorial model, a simulation-based evaluation layer is introduced to assess section occupation, intermediate-station waiting, platform-capacity pressure, running-time fluctuations, and delay propagation. Within this layered framework, conventional heuristics, quantum-inspired algorithms, and hybrid algorithms are compared on the same decision structure. The results show that the QUBO model can generate feasible candidate schemes after decoding, while the simulation layer clearly differentiates the operational performance of the competing algorithms under both normal and disturbed conditions. In the tested scenarios, QPSO-QAOA performs best under normal conditions, and the quantum-enhanced methods reduce comprehensive cost by 4.28\%--26.26\% and total delay by 4.37\%--24.25\% on average under dynamic conditions relative to their conventional counterparts. These findings suggest that the integration of QUBO-based modeling and simulation-based evaluation provides a useful methodological framework for railway short-term concentrated departure scheduling, although validation with real operational data remains necessary.
tldr: This paper applies QUBO and hybrid quantum algorithms to optimize railway departure sequencing and track allocation, with a simulation-based evaluation layer.
motivation: Efficient scheduling in railway concentrated departure scenarios is critical for reducing delays and operational costs, but static combinatorial models fail to capture time-dependent interactions.
method: A QUBO model is formulated for departure-position assignment and section-track selection, combined with a simulation-based evaluation layer to assess operational performance under normal and disturbed conditions.
result: Quantum-enhanced methods (QPSO-QAOA) reduce comprehensive cost by 4.28%–26.26% and total delay by 4.37%–24.25% compared to conventional heuristics.
conclusion: The QUBO+simulation framework is useful for railway scheduling, but validation with real data is needed.

title: High-Speed Multi-Dimensional Optical Field Measurement Via Mmf-mcf Spatial-Temporal Mapping Architecture
authors: Yuxuan Xiong, Jingze Liu, Junjie Qiu, Zhuyixiao Liu, Zheng Gao, Hao Wu, Ming Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wavelength and state of polarization constitute fundamental dimensions of optical fields. While simultaneous quantification of these parameters is critical, existing methodologies often lack the speed required for real-time analysis. Here, we present a compact high-dimensional optical field analyzer employing a discrete spatiotemporal sampling architecture based on multimode and multicore fibers. An optical delay line array maps spatial speckle patterns into serial pulse sequences and facilitates efficient single-pixel detection. Leveraging a residual multilayer perceptron network, the system attains a wavelength mean absolute error of 0.25 pm and a polarization resolution of 0.2015 (in normalized Stokes space). Analysis of the spatial sampling density reveals that 5-6 sampling points are required to balance measurement rate and accuracy. Notably, the system exhibits isotropic fault tolerance against single-core failures. This confirms that optical field information is redundantly encoded across the entire fiber cross-section rather than localized in specific channels. This framework provides a solution for multiparameter decoupling under severe spatial downsampling and useful insights for the design of next generation high-speed and robust all-fiber analysis systems.
tldr: A high-speed optical field analyzer using multimode-multicore fiber mapping and a neural network for wavelength and polarization measurement.
motivation: Existing methods for simultaneous quantification of wavelength and polarization lack the speed required for real-time analysis.
method: A discrete spatiotemporal sampling architecture based on multimode and multicore fibers maps spatial speckle patterns into serial pulse sequences, enabling single-pixel detection; a residual multilayer perceptron network decodes the parameters.
result: The system achieves a wavelength mean absolute error of 0.25 pm and a polarization resolution of 0.2015 in normalized Stokes space, with 5-6 sampling points balancing rate and accuracy.
conclusion: The framework provides a solution for multiparameter decoupling under spatial downsampling and offers insights for high-speed, robust all-fiber analysis systems.

title: Circular Raman Responses From Angular-momentum Inequivalence In CoSi
authors: Yuki Suganuma, Gakuto Kusuno, Kohei Miyazaki, Hikaru Watanabe, Rikuto Oiwa, Ryotaro Arita, Satoshi Iwasaki, Yoshiki Yasuoka, Yusuke Kousaka, Yoshihiko Togawa, Takuya Satoh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Circularly polarized Raman scattering in solids exhibits distinct phenomena such as Raman optical activity (ROA) and chiral-phonon-induced frequency splitting, whose relationship has remained unclear. Here we show that these seemingly different responses can be understood within a common framework based on the inequivalence of phonon states carrying opposite crystal angular momenta. Using helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy of the chiral crystal CoSi, we find that ROA and frequency splitting arise from different symmetry channels, namely axial multipolar symmetry and structural chirality, respectively. First-principles calculations reproduce both effects and clarify their symmetry origins. These results establish angular-momentum inequivalence as a unifying principle of circular Raman responses and link helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy to the angular-momentum structure of chiral phonons in topological materials.
tldr: This paper studies circular Raman responses in CoSi, linking Raman optical activity and chiral-phonon frequency splitting via angular-momentum inequivalence.
motivation: The relationship between Raman optical activity and chiral-phonon-induced frequency splitting in solids was unclear; the authors aimed to unify these phenomena.
method: Helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy on chiral crystal CoSi combined with first-principles calculations.
result: Raman optical activity and frequency splitting arise from different symmetry channels: axial multipolar symmetry and structural chirality, respectively.
conclusion: Angular-momentum inequivalence is a unifying principle for circular Raman responses, linking helicity-resolved Raman spectroscopy to chiral phonons in topological materials.

title: Frequency Detuning And Interference-Induced Bohmian Chaos In A Two-Dimensional Anisotropic Harmonic Oscillator
authors: Umair Abdul Halim, Nurisya Mohd Shah, Chan Kar Tim, Ahmad Hazazi Ahmad Sumadi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the emergence of chaotic Bohmian trajectories in a three-mode superposition of the ground and first excited states of a two-dimensional anisotropic harmonic oscillator. The analysis focuses on the interference-induced phase structure of the wavefunction, which determines the Bohmian velocity field through its phase gradient. We show that the spatial extent of chaotic motion is controlled by the temporal coherence of the interference pattern, set by the detuning between oscillator modes. Near resonance, slow beating generates long-lived phase-gradient structures that repeatedly stretch and fold nearby trajectories, leading to more spatially extended chaotic regions. In contrast, strong detuning produces rapid temporal decorrelation of the phase field and confines chaotic dynamics to localized regions of configuration space. To quantify this behavior, we use a dimensionless coherence parameter comparing the beating time scale with a characteristic transport time. The results identify temporal coherence of the interference-induced phase field as a useful diagnostic for chaotic transport in low-dimensional Bohmian systems.
tldr: This paper studies chaotic Bohmian trajectories in a two-dimensional anisotropic harmonic oscillator, focusing on the role of frequency detuning and interference-induced phase structures.
motivation: To understand how temporal coherence of interference patterns affects chaotic transport in Bohmian mechanics.
method: Analyzes a three-mode superposition of ground and first excited states, computes Bohmian velocity fields from phase gradients, and introduces a dimensionless coherence parameter comparing beating time to transport time.
result: Near resonance, slow beating leads to extended chaotic regions; strong detuning confines chaos to localized areas.
conclusion: Temporal coherence of the interference-induced phase field is a useful diagnostic for chaotic transport in low-dimensional Bohmian systems.

title: Laser-Stabilized Fiber Sensing On Terrestrial Field-Deployed Cable For Enhanced Sensitivity
authors: Rajiv Boddeda, Adrish Sahu, Christian Dorize, Arnaud Dupas, Pierre Brochard, Ha\"ik Mardoyan, Carina Castineiras, J\'er\'emie Renaudier
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07251v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate distributed acoustic sensing on deployed buried cable leveraging laser frequency stabilization and probing code optimization. Our results confirm the capability to accurately localize weak events with high resolution and sensitivity over 80 km.
tldr: Demonstrates distributed acoustic sensing on deployed fiber using laser stabilization and code optimization.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and localization of weak events in long-haul fiber for sensing applications.
method: Laser frequency stabilization and probing code optimization are applied to a field-deployed buried cable for distributed acoustic sensing.
result: Accurate localization of weak events with high resolution and sensitivity over 80 km is achieved.
conclusion: The approach enhances fiber sensing performance, but the work is purely classical optical sensing with no quantum component.

title: Variations On Majorization Of Vectors And Connections To Determinantal Inequalities
authors: Shaun Fallat, Samir Mondal, Hristo Sendov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Majorization is a fundamental tool for comparing vectors, with connections to convexity, doubly stochastic matrices, eigenvalues, singular values, and zeros of polynomials. In matrix analysis, it plays a central role in the study of eigenvalue inequalities, particularly those arising from classical determinantal inequalities such as those attributed to Hadamard and Fischer in the context of positive semidefinite matrices. A result of Fischer and Holbrook shows that equality in the Hardy--Littlewood--P\'olya theorem for non-affine convex functions is closely linked to block structure in the associated doubly stochastic transformations. Motivated by this, we introduce [MATH]-majorization, a structured extension of majorization that respects prescribed block decompositions of vectors. This framework naturally corresponds to block diagonal doubly stochastic matrices and provides a refinement of the classical Hardy--Littlewood--P\'olya and Rado theorem. We show that such transformations are precisely the linear operators that preserve [MATH]-majorization, and we extend fundamental constructions such as [MATH]-transforms and convex combinations to this setting. In an application, we study the eigenvalue relations associated with the principal submatrices of positive definite matrices. Classical majorization does not, in general, capture determinantal inequalities such as those of Koteljanskii, whereas [MATH]-majorization provides a natural framework for structured comparisons of eigenvalue vectors. This leads to new insights into the interplay between majorization theory, determinantal inequalities, and spectral properties of matrices.
tldr: This paper introduces a structured extension of majorization called M-majorization, which respects block decompositions of vectors, and applies it to determinantal inequalities for positive definite matrices.
motivation: Classical majorization does not capture certain determinantal inequalities like Koteljanskii's inequality; the authors aim to develop a refined majorization framework that naturally handles block-structured comparisons.
method: The authors define M-majorization based on block diagonal doubly stochastic matrices, characterize the linear operators preserving it, and extend classical constructions such as M-transforms and convex combinations.
result: M-majorization provides a natural framework for eigenvalue relations of principal submatrices of positive definite matrices, leading to new insights into determinantal inequalities.
conclusion: The work bridges majorization theory and matrix analysis, offering a structured tool for comparing vectors with applications to spectral properties.

title: Smooth Hard-Thresholding For Singular Values With Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate
authors: Guanzhong Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06632v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Low-rank matrix denoising is a central primitive in patch-based image restoration and many other inverse problems. Classical SVD-based image denoising methods often choose a truncation rank by matching residual singular-value energy with an estimated noise energy, but this rule is not a finite-sample risk principle because a fitted low-rank approximation inevitably absorbs part of the noise. This paper develops a mathematically rigorous alternative based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE). Since singular value hard thresholding is discontinuous and does not satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma, we introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator. We prove that the smooth shrinker satisfies the regularity conditions required by a spectral-estimator version of Stein's lemma, and therefore admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate under Gaussian noise. For a fixed observed matrix and a finite set of candidate thresholds separated from the observed singular values, the ordering of the fixed-threshold smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score. The limiting score has the same algebraic form as the biased hard-threshold SURE formula, but here it is used only as a computational device for ranking finite candidates. Selecting the minimizing threshold is a data-adaptive tuning step; the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the finally selected estimator.
tldr: This paper develops a smooth hard-thresholding estimator for singular values in low-rank matrix denoising, using Stein's unbiased risk estimate for threshold selection.
motivation: Classical SVD-based denoising methods lack a finite-sample risk principle; the paper aims to provide a rigorous alternative using SURE.
method: Introduces a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator that satisfies Stein's lemma regularity conditions, enabling an unbiased risk estimate under Gaussian noise.
result: Proves that the smooth shrinker admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate, and that the SURE objective ordering agrees with a simple limiting score for finite candidate thresholds.
conclusion: The method offers a data-adaptive threshold selection procedure, though the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the final estimator.

title: Data-driven Methods For Computation Of Optimal Linear Response In High-dimensional Dynamical Systems
authors: Gary Froyland, Dimitrios Giannakis, Nicholas Peters
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a data-driven framework for estimating optimal linear response of nonlinear dynamical systems. Our approach is based on kernel-smoothed approximations of the transfer/Koopman operators of the system, built from possibly high-dimensional observations along trajectories. Combining these operator approximations with the theory developed in [Antown et al. (2018), J. Stat. Phys., 170(6), 1051-1087], we formulate a computationally tractable optimization problem for the optimal infinitesimal perturbation realising any desired manipulation of the spectrum. We also introduce a notion of optimal-response vector fields for visualising, and physically interpreting, the system's response to the optimal perturbation under arbitrary observations. Our focus is on finding perturbations that optimally increase the frequency or optimally suppress the decay of correlations of almost-cycles or almost-invariant sets associated with the eigenvalues of the kernel-smoothed transfer operator. We illustrate our approach with applications to low-dimensional periodic and chaotic systems, as well as a high-dimensional example involving the El Nino Southern Oscillation in a comprehensive Earth system model. In these examples our approach discovers nontrivial optimal perturbations of the system, which are post hoc natural and consistent with the desired dynamical objectives.
tldr: A data-driven framework for computing optimal linear response in high-dimensional dynamical systems using kernel-smoothed approximations of transfer/Koopman operators.
motivation: To develop a computationally tractable method for finding optimal perturbations that manipulate the spectrum of nonlinear dynamical systems, with applications to climate phenomena like El Niño.
method: Kernel-smoothed approximations of transfer/Koopman operators from trajectory data are combined with optimization theory to find optimal infinitesimal perturbations.
result: The method discovers nontrivial optimal perturbations in low-dimensional chaotic systems and a high-dimensional Earth system model, consistent with desired dynamical objectives.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for optimal response analysis in complex systems, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multiscale Nudging: From Macroscopic Observations To Microscopic Dynamics
authors: Liyao Lyu, Xinyue Yu, Hayden Schaeffer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a measure-based nudging framework for assimilating macroscopic observations into microscopic mean-field particle dynamics. The central difficulty is a representation mismatch: the forecast is a labeled particle system, while the observations specify only a smoothed, permutation-invariant density.
